- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.3) over recent days, model tends to underpredict; adjust forecast upward by 1–2% to counteract pessimism.  
- After a sharp price spike (≥5% from prior peak), model often overreacts and overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above peak or use moving average to smooth.  
- If sentiment is high (≥0.7) and price is trending up, model frequently overestimates; reduce forecast by 1–3% to avoid overconfidence bias.  
- In mean-reversion scenarios (price near 30-day moving average), model often holds too long; apply early correction if sentiment drops below 0.4.  
- For 30-day horizon, model underperforms when sentiment is volatile (±0.25+ in 3-day window); use sentiment-weighted smoothing (e.g., 70% recent, 30% smoothed).  
- If sentiment is rising sharply (e.g., >0.15 increase in 3 days), model often fails to anticipate rally; add 0.5–1.5% buffer to forecast.
